title: USGS load limits retained a rise in phosphorus minus orthophosphate per sediment in two Gulf rivers, 1981-2025
abstract: We tested whether filtered orthophosphate alone accounts for the rise in total phosphorus per suspended sediment in two Gulf river load estimates. We used USGS version 3.0 and compared water years 1981-1996 with 2009-2025. Under stationary flow normalization, the orthophosphate term accounts for 29.79% of the point increase. The remaining phosphorus-minus-orthophosphate ratio rose from 0.505 to 1.050 mg P/g sediment, a factor of 2.081. If all annual loads lie within their published marginal limits at once, the exact rectangular factor bounds are 1.236 to 3.598. Rounding allowances retain a lower factor of 1.217. Thus an orthophosphate-only accounting explanation fails inside that box. This is not a joint confidence interval. The residual includes other dissolved forms and cannot be called particulate phosphorus. Separate river, method and period checks retain a residual rise. Shared fitted data, unknown joint model error and missing chemical fractions limit physical inference. Original code, aggregate results, a figure, exact source hashes and an independent Decimal audit are supplied. External source records are not bundled.

display.caption: Period ratios separate filtered orthophosphate from the remaining phosphorus load. Source-limit boxes retain an increase in the residual ratio. Boxes have no joint coverage probability.
